thread:
rachel.gtm: Quick heads-up — trying a tight pass on our competitive narrative for the launch next week. Need a short one-pager + 3 webinar hooks that call out differences vs cloud AI platforms, LLM APIs, and infra vendors. Can we iterate here?

samir.ae: On it. focusing on buyer objections: reliability, predictable cost, and rollout complexity.

maya.prod: + include a short customer-facing benchmark line: most folks care about median latency and token cost per 1k.

oliver.content: Draft idea for the one-pager header: "Serving-first inference: predictable latency, transparent unit economics, same API everywhere" — too long?

rachel.gtm: good. tighten: "Serving-first inference: predictable latency. predictable cost. predictable ops." small caps.

natalie.analytics: I ran a quick cohort map — for enterprise POCs the top 2 triggers are (1) SLA language and (2) demo latency under 200ms. We should call those out.

bench-bot: perf-scan: hosted_v1 median latency 180ms, dedicated_v2 median 95ms with caching on; token cost delta: hosted ~ $0.024/1k, dedicated optimized ~ $0.013/1k. (raw numbers for internal use)

samir.ae: Perfect — that'll help the 'econ' snip for SDRs. Can we make a 2-line objection handler: "Why not just use cloud AI endpoints?"

oliver.content: Proposal for objection handler lines: 1) "Cloud endpoints are easy — but they hide unit economics and tail latency under bursty load." 2) "Homegrown infra gives control but costs months of ops time; Redwood provides predictable throughput with rollout tooling."

maya.prod: Add fallback policy line: "Graceful degradation via model variants keeps user-facing latency in SLOs during regional pressure."

rachel.gtm: Nice. Now webinar hooks (3): 1) "How we shave 2x off inference cost without sacrificing latency" 2) "Real-world routing: keeping SLAs in multi-region bursts" 3) "From POC to scale: rollout strategies that don't break your product"

natalie.analytics: I'll produce two slides: one with the latency vs cost scatter, one with benchmark methodology (datasets, sequence lengths, batching). Keep the benchmark methodology short — folks distrust opaque tests.

bench-bot: sample blurb for slides: "Methodology: 10k real requests replay, mixed seq lengths (8–512), continuous batching, KV-cache enabled. Metrics: median, p95 latency, cost/token. Repro script: `scripts/repro/run_bench.sh`"

samir.ae: Can marketing give me a 3-sentence SDR opener using this?

oliver.content: SDR opener draft: "Hi — quick note: we help teams get consistent production latency and cut per-token inference cost — customers typically see 30–60% unit-cost reductions vs public endpoints while keeping median latency in the 100–200ms range. Happy to share a short report."

rachel.gtm: Clean — replace 'typically see' with 'often realize' and swap 30–60% for 'up to 60% depending on workload'.

oliver.content: Updated: "Hi — quick note: we help teams get consistent production latency and cut per-token inference cost — customers often realize up to 60% unit-cost reductions vs public endpoints while keeping median latency in the 100–200ms range. Happy to share a short report."

maya.prod: Next steps: oliver to draft one-pager + SDR snips by EOD, natalie to add two benchmark visuals by tomorrow noon, samir to run through objection handlers with two AE buddies and reply here, rachel to assemble webinar outline and send calendar invite.

samir.ae: Got it — I'll ping @leo and @anya for a quick sanity check.

rachel.gtm: Thanks all. If anyone has a must-avoid phrase (legal or competitive), call it out now. Otherwise we'll lock copy by EOD and ship to the field tomorrow. :rocket:

bench-bot: note: internal-only benchmark numbers above. Do not publish raw cost figures without approval. :warning:
